'''Brad Smelley''' (born April 20, 1989)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/stats/_/id/15055/brad-smelley |title=Brad Smelley Stats - Cleveland Browns - ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=April 20, 1989 |access-date=August 17, 2012}}</ref> is an American retired professional [[American football|football]] [[tight end]]. He was selected by the [[Cleveland Browns]] in the seventh round of the [[2012 NFL draft]]. He played college football at the [[University of Alabama]]. He was also a member of the [[Houston Texans]] and [[St. Louis Rams]].

==College career==
He played [[college football]] at [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama]], where he started at [[tight end]] and won two [[College football national championships in NCAA Division I FBS|NCAA National Championships]]. In his career, he had 54 receptions for 559 yards and four touchdowns.

==Professional career==

===Cleveland Browns===
Smelley was selected by the [[Cleveland Browns]] in the seventh round, 247th overall in the [[2012 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2012/draft.htm |access-date=May 14, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Brad was let go from the [[Cleveland Browns]] on August 31, 2012, and signed to the practice squad. On December 10, 2012, Smelley was signed to the Cleveland Browns active roster. <ref>{{cite web | last=Pokorny | first=Chris | title=Cleveland Browns Promote FB Brad Smelley to Roster | website=Dawgs By Nature |publisher=SB Nation| date=2012-12-10 | url=https://www.dawgsbynature.com/2012/12/10/3753482/cleveland-browns-promote-fb-brad-smelley-to-active-roster | access-date=2025-07-04}}</ref> On September 1, 2013, Smelley was cut by the Cleveland Browns and became a free agent.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cleveland.com/browns/index.ssf/2013/09/cleveland_browns_cut_brandon_j.html|title = Browns cut Brandon Jackson, Kellen Davis, Brad Smelley, LJ Fort, claim six|date = September 2, 2013}}</ref>

===St. Louis Rams (first stint)===
Smelley was signed to the St. Louis Rams practice squad in November, but was released three days later in favor of [[Justice Cunningham]].

===Houston Texans===
On December 3, 2013, Smelley signed with the [[practice squad]] of the [[Houston Texans]].<ref>{{cite web|work=CSNHouston.com|url=http://www.csnhouston.com/football-houston-texans/talk/texans-add-smelley-practice-squad|title=Texans add Smelley to practice squad|date=December 3, 2013|first=Dave|last=Zangaro|access-date=July 10, 2014|archive-date=July 15, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140715023151/http://www.csnhouston.com/football-houston-texans/talk/texans-add-smelley-practice-squad|url-status=dead}}</ref> The Texans promoted him to the active roster on December 13 but was later released by the team.<ref>{{cite news|work=NBCSports.com|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/12/13/texans-promote-tight-end-brad-smelley-from-practice-squad/|title=Texans promote tight end Brad Smelley from practice squad|first=Mike|last=Wilkening|date=December 13, 2013|access-date=July 10, 2014}}</ref>

===St. Louis Rams (second stint)===
Smelley was signed by the St. Louis Rams on August 11, 2014, to fill the void left by [[Mason Brodine]] after he was placed on injured reserve. He was released during final cuts on August 29, 2014. He was signed to the Rams practice squad on September 3, 2014.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.al.com/sports/index.ssf/2014/09/brad_smelley_gets_spot_on_st_l.html | title=Brad Smelley gets spot on St. Louis Rams practice squad | access-date=September 23, 2014 | author=Inabinett, Mark| date=September 4, 2014 }}</ref>

On January 6, 2015, Smelley signed a [[futures contract]] with the Rams.<ref>{{cite web|work=StLouisRams.com|url=http://www.stlouisrams.com/news-and-events/article-1/Palardy-Smelley-Signed-to-Futures-Contract/f07dc8a5-efb3-44f0-8171-11631fc2a5ab|title=Palardy, Smelley Signed to Futures Contract|date=January 6, 2015|first=Myles|last=Simmons|access-date=January 8, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151218083948/http://www.stlouisrams.com/news-and-events/article-1/Palardy-Smelley-Signed-to-Futures-Contract/f07dc8a5-efb3-44f0-8171-11631fc2a5ab|archive-date=December 18, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''Brad Herman''' is an American former [[American football|football]] [[tight end]].  He was born in [[Peoria, Illinois]] and moved to [[Metamora, Illinois]] in 2002{{citation needed|date=July 2012}} where he attended [[Metamora Township High School]].<ref name="hawkeye">{{cite web | url = http://www.hawkeyesports.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/herman_brad00.html | title = Brad Herman | work = hawkeyesports.com | publisher = [[CBS Interactive]] | accessdate = July 22, 2012 | url-status = dead | archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20120612025745/http://www.hawkeyesports.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/herman_brad00.html | archivedate = June 12, 2012 }}</ref>

==School sports==
In high school, in addition to playing football, Herman [[letterman (sports)|lettered]] in [[track and field|track]].<ref name="hawkeye"/>

During college, he played for [[Iowa Hawkeyes football]].<ref name="hawkeye"/>

==Professional football career==
The [[New England Patriots]] signed Herman as an undrafted free agent following the [[2012 NFL draft]].{{citation needed|date=July 2012}}  Herman tore his [[Achilles tendon]] during practice on June 5, was [[waivers (American football)|waived]], and was put on the [[injured reserve list]] on June 11, ending his playing for the season.<ref>{{cite news | url = http://www.bostonherald.com/blogs/sports/blitz/index.php/2012/06/11/patriots-place-brad-herman-on-injured-reserve/ | title = Patriots place Brad Herman on injured reserve | work = BostonHerald.com Sports | publisher = [[Boston Herald]] | date = June 11, 2012 <!-- , 5:16 pm  --> | accessdate = July 22, 2012 }}</ref> On April 29, 2013, the Patriots released Herman.

'''Bradley Mathias Kaaya Jr.''' (born September 3, 1995) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[quarterback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami Hurricanes]] from 2014 to 2016, and was selected by the [[Detroit Lions]] in sixth round of the [[2017 NFL draft]]. Kaaya is the [[Miami Hurricanes football statistical leaders|all time passing yards leader]] at Miami.

==Early life==
Kaaya attended [[Chaminade College Preparatory School (California)|Chaminade College Preparatory School]] in [[West Hills, Los Angeles]], [[California]], where he played [[high school football]] for the Eagles. As a senior, he threw for a school-record 3,855 yards and 27 [[touchdowns]]. During his high school career, he threw for 5,730 yards and 40 touchdowns while leading his school to their first ever CIF and CA State Championship (2013). He was ranked by the [[Rivals.com]] recruiting network as the eighth best pro-style [[quarterback]] recruit in his class and was also a member of Nike's [[Elite 11]], showcasing the top 11 quarterback recruits in the nation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brad Kaaya, 2014 Pro Style Quarterback, Miami (FL) |url=https://rivals.com/content/athletes/brad-kaaya-22543?view=pv |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Rivals.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

==College career==
Kaaya was named the Hurricanes starting quarterback as a true freshman over [[Jake Heaps]] by head coach [[Al Golden (American football)|Al Golden]] on August 24, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 24, 2014|agency=Associated Press |title=Brad Kaaya wins Miami Hurricanes quarterback job |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/11402524/brad-kaaya-wins-miami-quarterback-job |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Degnan |first=Susan Miller |date=August 24, 2014 |title=Brad Kaaya new starting QB for Miami Hurricanes – Eye on the U |url=http://miamiherald.typepad.com/umiami/2014/08/miami-hurricanes-new-starting-quarterback-is-.html |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Miami Herald}}</ref> Kaaya led the Hurricanes to a 6–7 overall record and a [[bowl game|bowl]] appearance, losing to [[2014 South Carolina Gamecocks football team|South Carolina]] in the [[2014 Independence Bowl]]. Kaaya was named [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] Rookie of the year following a 2014 regular season in which he led the league in pass efficiency and touchdown passes.<ref name="v380">{{cite web | title=Miami’s Kaaya Voted ACC Rookie Of The Year | website=Miami Hurricanes Athletics | date=2014-12-02 | url=https://miamihurricanes.com/news/2014/12/02/209791015-2/ | access-date=2024-09-28}}</ref> In his second year starting, the 2015 Hurricanes improved to 8–5, with a loss to [[2015 Washington State Cougars football team|Washington State]] in the [[2015 Sun Bowl|Sun Bowl]]. Kaaya had the 2016 Hurricanes off to their best start of his career, going 4–1 and reaching as high as #10 in the [[AP Poll]]. Miami finished the 2016 season with a 9–4 record and a win over [[2016 West Virginia Mountaineers football team|West Virginia]] in the [[2016 Russell Athletic Bowl]]. Kaaya was named bowl MVP and became Miami's all-time leader in nearly every passing statistic, including yards.

On January 2, 2017, Kaaya announced that he would be entering the [[2017 NFL draft]] rather than returning to Miami for his final season of eligibility.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Degnan |first=Susan Miller |date=January 3, 2017 |title=Brad Kaaya entering NFL draft |url=http://miamiherald.typepad.com/umiami/2017/01/brad-kaaya-.html |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Miami Herald}}</ref>

The [[Detroit Lions]] selected Kaaya in the sixth round (215th overall) of the [[2017 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Twentyman |first=Tim |date=April 29, 2017 |title=Detroit Lions draft defensive lineman Jeremiah Ledbetter |url=http://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-draft-weekend/article-1/Detroit-Lions-draft-defensive-lineman-Jeremiah-Ledbetter/98a9625b-5a0b-4d29-9202-5814a14b9fa4 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170430010157/http://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-draft-weekend/article-1/Detroit-Lions-draft-defensive-lineman-Jeremiah-Ledbetter/98a9625b-5a0b-4d29-9202-5814a14b9fa4 |archive-date=April 30, 2017 |access-date=April 29, 2017 |website=Detroit Lions}}</ref> He was the ninth quarterback selected in the draft.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2017/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> On May 12, 2017, the Lions signed Kaaya to a four-year, $2.52 million contract with a signing bonus of $123,352.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Brad Kaaya contract |url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/detroit-lions/brad-kaaya-21957/ |access-date=May 14, 2017 |website=spotrac.com}}</ref> He was waived by the Lions on September 2.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 2, 2017 |title=Lions establish 53-man roster |url=http://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-establish-53-man-roster/afd5f964-b8d1-4f20-8b0b-055acb8905ac |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170903005052/https://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-establish-53-man-roster/afd5f964-b8d1-4f20-8b0b-055acb8905ac |archive-date=September 3, 2017 |website=DetroitLions.com}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
On September 3, 2017, Kaaya was claimed off waivers by the [[Carolina Panthers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Henson |first=Max |date=September 3, 2017 |title=Panthers claim Brad Kaaya and Demetrious Cox |url=http://www.panthers.com/news/article-2/Panthers-claim-Brad-Kaaya-and-Demetrious-Cox/74b9ed41-5f37-4ce3-b8f1-b6d973c85fad |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171010225712/http://www.panthers.com/news/article-2/Panthers-claim-Brad-Kaaya-and-Demetrious-Cox/74b9ed41-5f37-4ce3-b8f1-b6d973c85fad |archive-date=October 10, 2017 |access-date=September 3, 2017 |website=Panthers.com}}</ref> He was waived by the Panthers on October 17.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Henson, Max |date=October 17, 2017 |title=Panthers sign LB Andrew Gachkar, waive QB Brad Kaaya |url=http://www.panthers.com/news/article-2/Panthers-sign-LB-Andrew-Gachkar-waive-QB-Brad-Kaaya/82760890-fb40-4877-87aa-4767971f0a6a |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171017202645/http://www.panthers.com/news/article-2/Panthers-sign-LB-Andrew-Gachkar-waive-QB-Brad-Kaaya/82760890-fb40-4877-87aa-4767971f0a6a |archive-date=October 17, 2017 |access-date=October 17, 2017 |website=Panthers.com}}</ref>

===Detroit Lions (second stint)===
On October 18, 2017, Kaaya was claimed off waivers by the Lions.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 18, 2017 |title=Lions sign free agents DE Jacquies Smith and T Bryce Harris |url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-sign-free-agents-de-jacquies-smith-and-t-bryce-harris-19599589 |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=DetroitLions.com}}</ref> On October 23, Kaaya was waived by the Lions and re-signed to the [[practice squad]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 23, 2017 |title=Lions activate DT Khyri Thornton from exempt-commissioner permission |url=http://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-activate-DT-Khyri-Thornton-from-exempt-commissioner-permission/96e78918-1149-47c7-9f4c-66032b29e6ed |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171024100621/http://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-activate-DT-Khyri-Thornton-from-exempt-commissioner-permission/96e78918-1149-47c7-9f4c-66032b29e6ed |archive-date=October 24, 2017 |access-date=October 24, 2017 |website=DetroitLions.com}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
On December 27, 2017, Kaaya was signed by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] off the Lions' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 27, 2017 |title=Roster Moves: Colts Sign QB Brad Kaaya; Place CB Rashaan Melvin On IR |url=http://www.colts.com/news/article-1/Roster-Moves-Colts-Sign-QB-Brad-Kaaya-Place-CB-Rashaan-Melvin-On-IR/f543c193-63f3-4dfa-ad45-1f1e3b9d2954 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171228000301/http://www.colts.com/news/article-1/Roster-Moves-Colts-Sign-QB-Brad-Kaaya-Place-CB-Rashaan-Melvin-On-IR/f543c193-63f3-4dfa-ad45-1f1e3b9d2954 |archive-date=December 28, 2017 |access-date=December 27, 2017 |website=Colts.com}}</ref>

On August 24, 2018, Kaaya was [[waived/injured]] by the Colts and placed on [[injured reserve]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 24, 2018 |title=Roster Moves: Colts Sign CB Juante Baldwin; Waive-Injured QB Brad Kaaya |url=https://www.colts.com/news/roster-moves-colts-sign-cb-juante-baldwin-waive-injured-qb-brad-kaaya |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Colts.com}}</ref> He was waived from injured reserve on February 8, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |author-link=Charean Williams |date=2019-02-08 |title=Colts cut Brad Kaaya |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/colts-cut-brad-kaaya |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Cincinnati Bengals===
On February 11, 2019, Kaaya was claimed off waivers by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sheeran |first=John |date=February 11, 2019 |title=Bengals claim Brad Kaaya off waivers from Colts |url=https://www.cincyjungle.com/2019/2/11/18220980/nfl-news-bengals-brad-kaaya-waivers-colts-free-agents |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Cincy Jungle|publisher=SB Nation}}</ref> However, the Bengals declined to assign him a [[restricted free agent]] tender for 2019, making Kaaya an unrestricted free agent at the start of the new league year in March.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 13, 2019 |title=Brad Kaaya: Non-tendered by Cincy |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/brad-kaaya-non-tendered-by-cincy/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Kaaya's mother, [[Angela Means]], is a [[vegan]] cook and former actress, who is best known for her role as Felisha in the 1995 classic film ''[[Friday (1995 film)|Friday]]'' as well as Veda in ''[[House Party 3]]'' and Aunt Vanessa in the TV series ''[[Cousin Skeeter]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Painter |first=Jill |date=July 21, 2014 |title=Bye, Felicia! Brad Kaaya, Miami QB, enjoys mom's phrase trending again 20 years later |url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20140721/bye-felicia-brad-kaaya-miami-qb-enjoys-moms-phrase-trending-again-20-years-later |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=[[Los Angeles Daily News]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Douglas |first=Stephen |date=February 5, 2014 |title=Miami Recruit Brad Kaaya's Mother Was an Actress Who Played "Felisha" in Friday |url=http://thebiglead.com/2014/02/05/miami-recruit-brad-kaaya-mother-actress-played-felisha-in-friday/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=The Big Lead}}</ref> His father Brad Kaaya Sr. coached him in Pop Warner football and is a former screenwriter who wrote for the film ''[[O (2001 film)|O]]'' and the TV series ''Cousin Skeeter'', ''[[Damon (TV series)|Damon]]'', and ''[[MADtv]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Solomon, Jon |date=August 12, 2016 |title=Raising Kaaya: Mom's fame, dad's obsessiveness shape Miami's star QB |url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/raising-kaaya-moms-fame-dads-obsessiveness-shape-miamis-star-quarterback/ |access-date=December 28, 2016 |website=CBS Sports}}</ref> His surname originates from [[Tanzania]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Porter |first=Matt |date=August 15, 2014 |title=Hurricanes QB Brad Kaaya impresses with preparedness, California cool |language=en |work=[[Palm Beach Post]] |url=http://www.mypalmbeachpost.com/sports/college-football/hurricanes-brad-kaaya-impresses-with-preparedness-california-cool/99VTeVIs89S3MTMFFPmWkI/ |access-date=September 18, 2017 |archive-date=October 19, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171019061255/http://www.mypalmbeachpost.com/sports/college-football/hurricanes-brad-kaaya-impresses-with-preparedness-california-cool/99VTeVIs89S3MTMFFPmWkI/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

'''Brad Bars''' (born April 24, 1992) is an American businessman and former [[American football]] [[linebacker]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] at [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State]].

== Early life ==
Attended Montgomery Bell Academy in [[Nashville, Tennessee]] where he played football, basketball, baseball, and track. As a junior and senior, he led the state of [[Tennessee]] in tackles (179), tackles for loss (32), and sacks (14) leading to two all state selections. Following his senior year, he was named an All-American (Max Emfinger). A three-star recruit by ESPN, he signed in 2010 to play football at [[Penn State]].

== College career ==
Bars played at Penn State, where he was a four-year letterman and four time Academic All Big Ten from 2011–2014.

== Professional career ==
Bars was ranked the 57th defensive lineman in the draft by nfldraftscout.com where he was projected to be a priority free agent. At Penn State pro day, Bars posted 4.68 40 yard dash, a 4.24 20-yard shuttle, and a 7.05 L cone. Bars also benched 225lbs 27 reps, and jumped 32" and 9'7" in the vertical and broad jump respectively.

After going undrafted in the [[2015 NFL draft]], Bars attended rookie minicamp with the New York Giants where he signed a contract on August 2, 2015. Bars recorded his first NFL tackle against the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] in Week 2. In Week 4 against the [[New England Patriots]], he recorded 3 tackles. After preseason, he was signed to the 10-man practice squad. On December 25, the [[New York Giants]] promoted Bars and [[tight end]] [[Matt LaCosse]] to the 53-man roster and placed [[Tackle (gridiron football position)|defensive tackle]] [[Markus Kuhn (American football)|Markus Kuhn]] and [[linebacker]] [[James Morris (American football)|James Morris]] on injured reserve.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=December 25, 2015 |title=DE Brad Bars and TE Matt LaCosse added to active roster |url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/DE-Brad-Bars-and-TE-Matt-LaCosse-added-to-active-roster/1400520b-03e3-4b98-9f07-fd0fff43f7f8 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151227192102/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/DE-Brad-Bars-and-TE-Matt-LaCosse-added-to-active-roster/1400520b-03e3-4b98-9f07-fd0fff43f7f8 |archive-date=December 27, 2015 |access-date=December 31, 2015 |website=Giants.com}}</ref>

On September 3, 2016, Bars was released by the Giants.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=September 3, 2016 |title=New York Giants announce 20 roster moves |url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-announce-20-roster-moves/d7b93d76-3186-40dc-b759-c622015e0159 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825063500/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-announce-20-roster-moves/d7b93d76-3186-40dc-b759-c622015e0159 |archive-date=August 25, 2017 |website=Giants.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Bars' brother, [[Alex Bars|Alex]], played in the NFL from 2019 to 2022 for the [[Chicago Bears]] and [[Las Vegas Raiders]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Bars family of Nashville fills a huddle | website=USA Today High School Sports | date=2012-12-25 | url=https://www.usatodayhss.com/story/sports/high-school/2012/12/25/bars-family-of-nashville-fills-a-huddle/81368255007/ | access-date=2025-10-12}}</ref>

'''Bradford Timothy Davis''' (born February 9, 1953) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] for two seasons with the [[Atlanta Falcons]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[LSU Tigers football|LSU Tigers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Brad Davis NFL Football Statistics|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DaviBr20.htm|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|access-date=April 14, 2016}}</ref>

He rushed for 2,253 yards on 472 carries in his college career, and had 16 rushing and two receiving touchdowns.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brad Davis Stats|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/brad-davis-1.html|website=Sports-Reference.com|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|access-date=April 24, 2016}}</ref> He was named to the [[1973 All-SEC football team|1973 All-SEC team]] as a first-team selection by the [[United Press]] and second-team by the [[Associated Press]] after rushing for 904 yards and scoring seven total touchdowns during the season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1873&dat=19731206&id=eW4pAAAAIBAJ&pg=989,2355125&hl=en|work=Daytona Beach Morning Journal|title=3 Gators Named All-SEC|date=December 6, 1973|access-date=April 24, 2016|via=[[Google news archive]]}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/2567307/the_galveston_daily_news/|work=Galveston Daily News|date=November 30, 1973|page=9|access-date=April 24, 2016|title=Alabama Dominates All-SEC Team|author=David Moffit|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref>

'''Brad Jamar Ford''' (born January 11, 1974) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] for the [[Detroit Lions]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]] and was selected by the Lions in the fourth round of the [[1996 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1996 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1996/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-30 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

==College career==
Ford initially attended [[Fresno City College]] in 1992 and 1993, before transferring to the [[University of Alabama]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/playerf/ford00250.html |title=Brad Ford |website=TheProfFootballArchives.com |access-date=January 24, 2017 |archive-date=February 2, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202013948/http://www.profootballarchives.com/playerf/ford00250.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> At Alabama, he appeared in 23 games and recorded two [[interception]]s, one returned for a [[touchdown]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brad Ford College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/brad-ford-1.html |access-date=2025-10-04 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Professional career==

'''Bradley Seaton''' (born November 23, 1993) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Villanova Wildcats football|Villanova Wildcats]].

==Professional career==
===Tennessee Titans===
Seaton was selected by the [[Tennessee Titans]] in the seventh round, 236th overall, in the [[2017 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Select Villanova OT Brad Seaton in 7th Round|url=http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-4/Titans-Select-Villanova-OT-Brad-Seaton-in-7th-Round/dfdc9dd3-7fd9-41b1-a518-2faaace7bdd2|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TitansOnline.com|date=April 29, 2017|accessdate=May 20, 2017}}</ref> He was waived on September 2, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Down to 53 Players: A Position-by-Position Look|url=http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-4/Titans-Down-to-53-Players-A-Position-by-Position-Look/d201b599-31f7-4441-8f65-948795805f04|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TitansOnline.com|date=September 2, 2017|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180206112407/http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-4/Titans-Down-to-53-Players-A-Position-by-Position-Look/d201b599-31f7-4441-8f65-948795805f04|archivedate=February 6, 2018}}</ref> He was re-signed to the [[practice squad]] on September 20, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Sign WR Zach Pascal, Place LB Aaron Wallace on IR|url=http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-4/Titans-Sign-WR-Zach-Pascal-Place-LB-Aaron-Wallace-on-IR/d4e96f27-6052-410f-ab9f-0ea23a64c998|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180125233554/http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-4/Titans-Sign-WR-Zach-Pascal-Place-LB-Aaron-Wallace-on-IR/d4e96f27-6052-410f-ab9f-0ea23a64c998|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 25, 2018|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TitansOnline.com|date=September 20, 2017}}</ref> He was released on November 9, 2017.<ref>{{cite web |title= Titans sign OL Tyler Marz, release Brad Seaton |url= https://247sports.com/nfl/tennessee-titans/article/titans-sign-ol-tyler-marz-release-brad-seaton-110189674/ |website= 247Sports.com |date= November 9, 2017}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers (first stint)===
On November 29, 2017, Seaton was signed to the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dotson, Marpet to IR Among Multiple Moves|url=http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Dotson-Marpet-to-IR-Among-Multiple-Moves/fc51c8ef-97fe-4e9f-acc9-5ad9569388cb|author=Smith, Scott|website=Buccaneers.com|date=November 29, 2017|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180103003945/http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Dotson-Marpet-to-IR-Among-Multiple-Moves/fc51c8ef-97fe-4e9f-acc9-5ad9569388cb|archivedate=January 3, 2018}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the Buccaneers on January 3, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bucs Sign Eight to Futures Contracts|url=http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Bucs-Sign-Eight-to-Futures-Contracts/5357cf6e-d600-4a4d-99f6-81500dd4bdab|author=Smith, Scott|website=Buccaneers.com|date=January 3, 2018|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180308005623/http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Bucs-Sign-Eight-to-Futures-Contracts/5357cf6e-d600-4a4d-99f6-81500dd4bdab|archivedate=March 8, 2018}}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===
The [[Cleveland Browns]] signed Seaton to their practice squad on September 4, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Browns sign OL Brad Seaton to practice squad|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-sign-ol-brad-seaton-to-practice-squad|website=ClevelandBrowns.com|date=September 4, 2018}}</ref> The Browns signed Seaton to a futures contract on January 2, 2019.<ref>{{cite news |title=Browns sign nine players |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-sign-nine-players |publisher=ClevelandBrowns.com |date=January 2, 2019}}</ref> Seaton was waived by the Browns on August 31, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Browns cut roster to 53 players|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-cut-roster-to-53-players|website=ClevelandBrowns.com|date=August 31, 2019}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers (second stint)===
On September 1, 2019, Seaton was signed to the Buccaneers practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bucs Claim RB T.J. Logan, Add Two to Practice Squad|url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-claim-rb-t-j-logan-add-two-to-practice-squad-roster-move|author=Smith, Scott|website=Buccaneers.com|date=September 2, 2019}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the Buccaneers on December 30, 2019.

On August 6, 2020, Seaton opted out of the 2020 season due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite news |author=Smith, Scott |title=Raymond Calais' Return Among Bucs' Roster Moves |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/raymond-calais-roster-moves-mj-stewart-training-camp |website=Buccaneers.com |date=August 6, 2020 |accessdate=August 10, 2020}}</ref><ref name="s263">{{cite web | last=Patra | first=Kevin | title=What we learned from Buccaneers win over Chiefs in Super Bowl LV | website=NFL.com | date=2021-02-08 | url=https://www.nfl.com/news/what-we-learned-from-buccaneers-win-over-chiefs-in-super-bowl-lv | access-date=2024-12-29}}</ref> Without him, the Buccaneers went on to win [[Super Bowl LV]].

On August 31, 2021, Seaton was waived/injured by the Buccaneers and placed on [[injured reserve]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ryan Griffin, Antonio Hamilton Among Bucs' Cuts to Get to 53|url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/buccaneers-53-man-roster-cut-down-training-camp-2021-transactions|author=Smith, Scott|website=Buccaneers.com|date=September 1, 2021}}</ref> He was released on October 21.

On April 19, 2022, Seaton announced his retirement.<ref>{{cite web | title=Brad Seaton: Announces retirement | website=CBSSports.com | date=2022-04-19 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/brad-seaton-announces-retirement/ | access-date=2025-08-06}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://sportsforecaster.com/nfl/p/120552 | title=Brad Seaton Stats, Profile, Bio, Analysis and More | Retired | Sports Forecaster }}</ref>

'''Brad Cousino''' (born April 5, 1953) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Cousino, an undersized nose tackle, played [[college football]] for the [[Miami RedHawks football|Miami RedHawks]]. There he played for Dick Crum. He was the defensive MVP, leading Miami to an 11–1 record in 1975. Miami finished the season ranked 12th in the AP Poll, after defeating the University of South Carolina in the Tangerine Bowl. He was the undrafted in 1975 but made the Cincinnati Bengals team. He played for the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] in 1975, the [[New York Giants]] in 1976 and for the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] in 1977.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CousBr20.htm |title=Brad Cousino Stats |publisher=Pro-Football-Reference.com |date= |access-date=2018-09-02}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/player/bradcousino/2512074/profile |title=Brad Cousino, LB |work=Nfl.com |date= |access-date=2018-09-02}}</ref>

He played [[college football]] for the [[Eastern Illinois Panthers football|Eastern Illinois Panthers]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FichBr20.htm |title=Brad Fichtel Stats |work=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]] |access-date=June 23, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/players/brad-fichtel/ |title=Brad Fichtel, C |work=[[NFL.com]] |access-date=June 23, 2021}}</ref> and was inducted into the school's Hall of Fame in 2014.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/80129861/journal-gazette/|newspaper=Journal Gazette Times Courier | location=[[Mattoon, Illinois]] | date=May 2, 2014|title=Eastern Illinois University adding six to Hall of Fame | page=B1 | via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref>

He was selected by the Los Angeles Rams in the [[1993 NFL draft]] and was on the team for two years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1993 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1993/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-31 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name="nflpe"/> He played one game in his career, a week ten victory over the [[Denver Broncos]] in 1994.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Brad Fichtel Career Game Log|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FichBr20/gamelog|access-date=June 23, 2021|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com|language=en}}</ref> He attended football camp for the [[Washington Redskins]] in 1995, and almost joined the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in 1996, but failed a physical.<ref name="nflpe"/><ref name="blue"/>

Since then he became a physical education teacher in [[Heath, Texas]], and was a finalist for [[NFL Teacher of the Year]] in 2012.<ref name="nflpe"/><ref name="blue"/> He got his Master of Science in education at [[Canisius College]] in 2016.<ref name="trust"/> In 2018, he transitioned to the [[Rockwall Independent School District]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.rockwallisd.com/cms/lib3/TX02215269/Centricity/Domain/47/June%2025%202018%20RS.pdf | title=Rockwall Independent School District Board of Trustees Meeting – June 25, 2018 Regular Session | date=June 2018 | work=[[Rockwall Independent School District]]  | access-date=June 23, 2021 }}</ref>

Fichtel is married to Suzanne, a former assistant district attorney in [[Rockwall, Texas]]. They have three sons.<ref name="blue"/> one who is following in his father's footsteps continuing his football career at Eastern Illinois

'''Boye Mafe''' (born November 30, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive end]] for the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Minnesota Golden Gophers football|Minnesota Golden Gophers]]. Mafe won [[Super Bowl LX]] with the [[Seattle Seahawks]].

==Early life==
Mafe's parents, Wale and Bola, came to the United States from [[Nigeria]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lynch |first=Evan |date=April 15, 2022 |title=Possible Ravens Draft Target Boye Mafe Proud Of Nigerian Heritage, On-Field Versatility |work=PressBoxOnline |url=https://pressboxonline.com/2022/04/15/possible-ravens-draft-target-boye-mafe-proud-of-nigerian-heritage-on-field-versatility/ |access-date=April 30, 2022}}</ref> Mafe grew up in [[Golden Valley, Minnesota]] and attended [[Hopkins High School]] in [[Minnetonka, Minnesota]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greder |first=Andy |date=December 18, 2020 |title=Gophers defensive end Boye Mafe's stock climbing on and off field. His late mother would be proud |url=https://www.bemidjipioneer.com/sports/football/6808939-Gophers-defensive-end-Boye-Mafe%E2%80%99s-stock-climbing-on-and-off-field.-His-late-mother-would-be-proud |access-date=September 29, 2021 |website=[[The Bemidji Pioneer]]}}</ref> As a senior he was named All-Metro after recording 78 tackles, 10 tackles for loss, and four sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shaver |first=Randy |date=November 18, 2016 |title=KARE 11 All-Metro Team 2016: Defense |url=https://www.kare11.com/article/sports/high-school/kare-11-all-metro-team-2016-defense/353888735 |access-date=September 29, 2021 |website=[[KARE (TV)|KARE.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Foster |first=Brandon |date=May 14, 2016 |title=2017 Wyoming target: Boye Mafe |url=https://trib.com/sports/college/wyoming/football/2017-wyoming-target-boye-mafe/article_3b30772a-515e-577a-a5a8-bacb7743f5c0.html |access-date=September 29, 2021 |website=[[Casper Star-Tribune]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Mafe [[redshirted]] his true freshman season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Irvin |first=Phil |date=November 11, 2020 |title=Defensive end Boye Mafe is a potential blueprint for sustained success at Minnesota |url=https://saturdaytradition.com/minnesota-football/defensive-end-boye-mafe-is-a-potential-blueprint-for-sustained-success-at-minnesota/ |access-date=September 29, 2021 |website=SaturdayTradition.com}}</ref> As a redshirt sophomore he recorded 14 tackles, 3.5 tackles for loss, and three sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fuller |first=Marcus |date=October 22, 2020 |title=Boye Mafe brings tremendous athletic ability to Gophers defensive line |url=https://www.startribune.com/boye-mafe-brings-tremendous-athletic-ability-to-gophers-defensive-line/572824842/ |access-date=September 29, 2021 |website=[[Star Tribune]]}}</ref> Mafe was named honorable mention [[List of All-Big Ten Conference football teams|All-Big Ten Conference]] after recording 27 tackles, 5.5 for loss, and 4.5 sacks with two passes defended and two forced fumbles in six games played in the team's [[COVID-19]]-shortened [[2020 NCAA Division I FBS football season|2020 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Baird |first=Nathan |date=July 3, 2021 |title=Minnesota's 'freakish' Boye Mafe out to ruin Ohio State quarterback's debut: Buckeyes' best opponents, No. 18 |url=https://www.cleveland.com/osu/2021/07/minnesotas-freakish-boye-mafe-out-to-ruin-ohio-state-quarterbacks-debut-buckeyes-best-opponents-no-18.html |access-date=September 29, 2021 |website=[[Cleveland.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Greder |first=Andy |date=September 23, 2021 |title=Gophers' Boye Mafe had slow start, but he and Thomas Rush broke out vs. Colorado |url=https://www.twincities.com/2021/09/23/gophers-boye-mafe-had-slow-start-but-he-and-thomas-rush-broke-out-vs-colorado/ |access-date=September 29, 2021 |website=[[St. Paul Pioneer Press]]}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks===
Mafe was drafted 40th overall by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in the second round of the [[2022 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2022/draft.htm |access-date=May 20, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> The Seahawks acquired the 40th overall selection from the [[Denver Broncos]] in the [[Russell Wilson]] trade.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=April 29, 2022 |title=Seahawks Select Minnesota LB Boye Mafe With 40th Overall Pick |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/boye-mafe-nfl-draft-pick-40-lb-minnesota |access-date=May 2, 2022 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref> Mafe recorded his first career sack in Week 2 of his rookie season against the San Francisco 49ers.<ref>{{cite web |last=Taylor |first=Diane |date=2022-09-20 |title=Rookie spotlight: Boye Mafe shows up big against the 49ers |url=https://www.fieldgulls.com/2022/9/20/23362751/seattle-seahawks-rookie-spotlight-boye-mafe-shows-up-big-against-the-49ers-nfl-week-2 |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Field Gulls |publisher=SB Nation}}</ref> He finished his rookie season with three sacks and 41 total tackles (28 solo).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Boye Mafe 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MafeBo00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

In week 10 of the 2023 season, Mafe recorded a sack against [[Sam Howell]] in a 29–26 victory over the [[Washington Commanders]], setting a franchise record for the most sacks in consecutive games with seven.<ref name="b463">{{cite web | last=Obee | first=Maliik | title=Boye Mafe Etches Name In Franchise Record Books In Seahawks’ 29-26 Win Over Commanders | website=Seahawks.com| date=2023-11-13 | url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/boye-mafe-etches-name-in-franchise-record-books-in-seahawks-29-26-win-over-comma | access-date=2024-11-28}}</ref> In Week 16, against the Tennessee Titans, he had his first game with two sacks in the 20–17 win.<ref>{{cite web | last=Solms | first=Leonard | title=Boye Mafe keeps Seahawks in prime position for Wild Card berth | website=ESPN.com | date=2023-12-27 | url=https://www.espn.com/espn/story/_/id/39190524/boye-mafe-keeps-seahawks-prime-position-wild-card-berth | access-date=2026-02-15}}</ref> He finished the 2023 season with nine sacks, 52 total tackles (35 solo), six passes defended, one forced fumble, and two fumble recoveries.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Boye Mafe 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MafeBo00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Mafe started off the 2024 season with three consecutive games with a sack before missing Weeks 4–5 with a knee injury.<ref>{{cite web | last=Benintendi | first=Connor | title=Reviewing Projections: Boye Mafe in 2024 | website=Seattle Seahawks On SI | date=2025-01-15 | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/seahawks/onsi/seahawks-news/reviewing-projections-did-seahawks-edge-boye-mafe-disappoint-in-2024 | access-date=2026-02-15}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last=Smith | first=Corbin | title=Seattle Seahawks LB Boye Mafe Among Inactives vs. New York Giants | website=Seattle Seahawks On SI | date=2024-10-06 | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/seahawks/onsi/game-day/seattle-seahawks-lb-boye-mafe-among-inactives-vs-new-york-giants | access-date=2026-02-15}}</ref> He finished the 2024 season with six sacks, 40 total tackles (25 solo), and three passes defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Boye Mafe 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MafeBo00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

In the 2025 season, Mafe had two sacks, 31 total tackles (11 solo), and five passes defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Boye Mafe 2025 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MafeBo00/gamelog/2025/ |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Mafe played in Super Bowl LX.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LX - Seattle Seahawks vs. New England Patriots - February 8th, 2026 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202602080nwe.htm |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He won his first NFL championship when the Seahawks defeated the Patriots 29–13.<ref>{{cite web | last=Maaddi | first=Rob | title=Seahawks ride their 'Dark Side' defense to a Super Bowl title, pounding the Patriots 29-13 | website=AP News | date=2026-02-08 | url=https://apnews.com/article/super-bowl-seahawks-patriots-24ad67503a342a7e24348e66986250ab | access-date=2026-02-15}}</ref>

===Cincinnati Bengals===
On March 12, 2026, Mafe signed a three-year deal with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] worth $60 million, with $19 million guaranteed.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bengals Sign EDGE Boye Mafe BENGALS ROSTER UPDATE| website=[[Cincinnati Bengals]] | date=2026-03-12 | url=https://www.bengals.com/news/boye-mafe-three-year-contract-signed-2026-free-agency| access-date=2026-03-12}}</ref>

He was a third-team all-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] selection in 2021.{{cite news |author1=Aaron McMann |title=Michigan's Brad Hawkins 'frustrated' by combine snub, but eager for NFL shot |url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2022/03/michigans-brad-hawkins-frustrated-by-combine-snub-but-eager-for-nfl-shot.html |access-date=1 October 2022 |work=[[Michigan Live]] |date=22 March 2022}} ==Professional career== ===Atlanta Falcons=== After going undrafted in the [[2022 NFL draft]], Hawkins signed with the [[Atlanta Falcons]] as a free agent. He was cut by the Falcons on July 6, 2022.{{cite news |author1=Aaron McMann |title=Undrafted Michigan DB cut by Atlanta Falcons |url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2022/07/undrafted-michigan-db-cut-by-atlanta-falcons.html |access-date=4 October 2022 |work=[[Michigan Live]] |date=6 July 2022}} ===New England Patriots=== On August 2, 2022, Hawkins signed with the [[New England Patriots]].{{cite news |author1=Trent Knoop |title=Brad Hawkins lands an NFL deal |url=https://wolverineswire.usatoday.com/2022/08/01/michigan-football-brad-hawkins-signs-with-new-england-patriots/ |access-date=4 October 2022 |work=Wolverines Wire |publisher=[[USA Today]] |date=1 August 2022}} He was waived during final roster cuts on August 30.{{Cite web |date=August 30, 2022 |title=Patriots Make Roster Moves to Reach 53-Man Roster Limit |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-make-roster-moves-to-reach-53-man-roster-limit |access-date=February 19, 2023 |website=Patriots.com}} Though primarily signed for practice squad use, he played in the Patriots three preseason games. Hawkins was cut from the team on October 3.(5 October 2022). [https://www.si.com/nfl/patriots/news/new-england-roster-cuts-tracker-bill-belichick-mac-jones-patriots-pat-cannon New England Patriots Sign OL Marcus Cannon To Active Roster: NFL Tracker], ''Sports Illustrated'' He signed a reserve/future contract on January 10, 2023.{{cite web|title=Patriots sign 11 players to future contracts|url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-sign-11-players-to-future-contracts-x6434|website=Patriots.com|date=January 10, 2023}} Hawkins was released by the Patriots on August 27.{{cite web|title=Patriots Release 11 Players|url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-release-11-players|website=Patriots.com|date=August 27, 2023}} ==Coaching career== On March 4, 2024, Hawkins was hired by the [[Michigan Wolverines football|University of Michigan]] as a graduate assistant.{{cite web | last=Sayfie | first=Clayton | title=Michigan coach Sherrone Moore hires two new defensive staffers, one an NFL coach | website=The Wolverine | date=March 4, 2024 | url=https://www.on3.com/teams/michigan-wolverines/news/michigan-football-hires-kevin-wilkins-brad-hawkins/ | access-date=June 26, 2026}} == References == {{reflist}} ==External links== * [https://mgoblue.com/sports/football/roster/brad-hawkins/21993 Michigan player profile] {{DEFAULTSORT:Hawkins, Brad}} [[Category:1998 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American football defensive backs]] [[Category:New England Patriots players]] [[Category:Michigan Wolverines football coaches]] [[Category:Michigan Wolverines football players]] [[Category:Camden High School (New Jersey) alumni]] [[Category:Suffield Academy alumni]] [[Category:Players of American football from Camden, New Jersey]] [[Category:Coaches of American football from New Jersey]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]]

'''Brad Robbins''' (born October 6, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Punter (gridiron football)|punter]] for the [[Columbus Aviators]] of the [[United Football League (2024–present)|United Football League]] (UFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]], and was selected by the Bengals in the sixth round of the [[2023 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Rapien |first=James |date=April 29, 2023 |title=Bengals Take Michigan Punter Brad Robbins in Sixth Round of 2023 NFL Draft |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/bengals/news/bengals-take-michigan-punter-brad-robbins-in-sixth-round-of-2023-nfl-draft |access-date=September 8, 2023 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref>

==College career==
Robbins committed to [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan]] in February 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wenzel |first=Matt  |date=February 13, 2017 |title=Nation's No. 1 punter Brad Robbins took 30 seconds to commit to Michigan |url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2017/02/nations_no_1_punter_brad_robbi.html |access-date=September 8, 2023 |website=mlive.com}}</ref>

===Cincinnati Bengals===
Robbins was selected by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] in the sixth round (217th overall) of the [[2023 NFL draft]], making him and Michigan teammate [[Jake Moody]] the second punter and kicker tandem to be taken in the same draft in the last 40 years.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Brandon |date=April 30, 2023 |title=Jake Moody, Brad Robbins Make History |url=https://www.si.com/college/michigan/.amp/football/michigan-football-nfl-draft-jim-harbaugh-jake-moody-brad-robbins |access-date=May 1, 2023 |website=Wolverine Digest|publisher=Sports Illustrated}}</ref> He was the second punter taken in the draft behind [[Bryce Baringer]], and ahead of [[Ethan Evans]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2023/draft.htm |access-date=2024-07-21 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Robbins began the 2024 season on injured reserve with a quadriceps injury.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bengals Reduce Final Roster To 53 Players|url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-reduce-final-roster-to-53-players|website=Bengals.com|date=August 27, 2024}}</ref> He was released on October 1, 2024.<ref>{{cite web | last=Morrison | first=Jay | title=Cincinnati Bengals Waive Punter Brad Robbins as Ryan Rehkow Leads NFL in Gross, Net Average | website=SI.com| date=2024-10-01 | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/bengals/news/cincinnati-bengals-waive-punter-brad-robbins-as-ryan-rehkow-leads-nfl-in-gross-net-average-01j9430zw8wh | access-date=2025-06-30}}</ref>

===Buffalo Bills===
On March 31, 2025, Robbins signed with the [[Buffalo Bills]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kowle |first=Tam |date=31 March 2025 |title=Buffalo Bills sign punter Brad Robbins |url=https://billswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/bills/2025/03/31/buffalo-bills-sign-punter-brad-robbins-nfl/82744795007/ |access-date=1 April 2025 |website=Bills Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://buffalonews.com/sports/professional/nfl/bills/article_35521228-014e-4b81-9533-fc5a8978417b.html|title=Meet the Bills' contestants for Puntapalooza: Brad Robbins and Jake Camarda|date=June 17, 2025|agency=''[[The Buffalo News]]''|author=Lysowski, Lance|accessdate=June 20, 2025|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250617125524/https://buffalonews.com/sports/professional/nfl/bills/article_35521228-014e-4b81-9533-fc5a8978417b.html|archivedate=June 17, 2025}}</ref>
On September 9, he was released following their first game of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Glab |first=Maddy |date=9 September 2025 |title=Bills sign K Matt Prater and P Cameron Johnston, release P Brad Robbins |url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/bills-sign-k-matt-prater-and-p-cameron-johnston-release-p-brad-robbins |access-date=2025-09-09 |website=buffalobills.com}}</ref>

===Las Vegas Raiders===
On October 7, 2025, Robbins signed with the [[Las Vegas Raiders]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |title=Raiders sign P Brad Robbins to the practice squad |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-p-brad-robbins-to-the-practice-squad-release-lb-germaine-pratt |website=raiders.com |access-date=8 October 2025}}</ref> He was released on October 14.<ref>{{cite web |title=Raiders sign G McClendon Curtis to the practice squad |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-g-mcclendon-curtis-to-the-practice-squad-release-brad-robbins |website=raiders.com |access-date=15 October 2025}}</ref>

=== Columbus Aviators ===
On March 18, 2026, Robbins signed with the [[Columbus Aviators]] of the [[United Football League (2024–present)|United Football League]] (UFL). <ref>{{Cite web |last=Heilman |first=Michael |date=2026-03-19 |title=Columbus Aviators sign DE Quashon Fuller and Punter Brad Robbins |url=https://www.bgmsportstrax.com/2026/03/18/columbus-aviators-sign-de-quashon-fuller-and-punter-brad-robbins/ |access-date=2026-03-19 |website=BGMSportsTrax |language=en-US}}</ref>
